APCTT-C01.quote: This MPE product maintains the high spatial and temporal resolution of the NEXRAD precipitation estimates while incorporating the accuracy of ground-based point observations.
APCTT-C01.note: Basis of the multisensor estimates and of the Huff (1990) rainfall distributions used to disaggregate forecasts.

APCTT-C02.quote: The DuPage County streamflow simulation system uses these quantitative precipitation forecast data to create streamflow predictions for the two simulated drainage basins.
APCTT-C02.note: Application and how the processed data are used.

APCTT-C03.note: The report documents the processing steps; no analytical results of the pipeline are shown.

APCTT-C05.note: No validation of the processed precipitation against observations is reported.

APCTT-C06.quote: As part of this effort, the U.S. Geological Survey maintains a database of hourly meteorological and hydrologic data for use in this near real-time streamflow simulation system.
APCTT-C06.note: The pipeline runs for the real county basins inside the simulation system.

APCTT-C07.quote: The U.S. Geological Survey, in cooperation with DuPage County Stormwater Management Department, is testing a near real-time streamflow simulation system that assists in the management and operation of reservoirs and other flood-control structures in the Salt Creek and West Branch DuPage River drainage basins in DuPage County, Illinois.
APCTT-C07.note: Prototype being tested in the actual operational setting (near-real-time support of reservoir operations).

APCTT-C08.note: The system is still being tested; no qualification.

APCTT-C09.note: No record of successful operation over a period.

APCTT-C11.quote: The NWS QPF file used in the flood-simulation system contains the forecasted 6-hour precipitation totals and are typi-cally available for 72 hours.
APCTT-C11.note: Inputs, grid cells, subbasins and contribution factors are defined.

APCTT-C12.quote: This report documents the processes used by the U.S. Geological Survey to create basin-mean and subbasin model-input pre-cipitation time-series data using the next generation weather radar-multisensor precipitation estimates product.
APCTT-C12.note: Evidence concerns the processing pipeline itself.
